messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service=redwood-runtime-prod region=us-west-2 — sudden p95 spike and KV-cache page-in rate > 300/s, paging rising. Pager: @elaine oncall.
elaine: seeing big tail latency. p95 jumped from 80ms -> 1.2s in last 2m. cpu rps OK but gpus showing long stall periods. kv cache entries exploding.
mike: logs show repeated cache miss thrash + many long-context requests holding KV locks. example traces: https://trace.redwood/abc123
sophie: can you paste the cache metrics? I'm seeing page faults on the nvm loader.
earline: metrics snippet:
```
kv_cache_entries: 12.3M -> 98.6M (5m)
kv_cache_pages_in/s: 45 -> 340
continuous_batching_queue_len: 18 -> 210
p50/p95/p99: 60ms / 1.2s / 2.6s
gpu_mem_used_pct: 78 -> 96
```
raj: confirmed some tenants sending long-horizon generation requests (60k token windows) mixed with many short chat completions. Scheduler is favoring large requests causing starvation for small ones.
elaine: impact: several customer sessions reporting timeouts and elevated error rates. Support ticket surge: https://support.redwood/t/8765 — mark high-priority.
support: flagged 3 enterprise customers with SLA risk, their workflows hit p99 > 5s. We notified account owners.
infra-bot: OOM risk: node-43 nvme write latency rising; spooler backlog = 14k.
dave: I'm patching a quick mitigation: limit continuous_batching.max_window_tokens to 8k and reduce per-request max_batch_tokens to 4096 for host pool in us-west-2. Applying now.
elaine: please include the hotfix command.
dave: running:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap batching-config -p '{"data":{"max_window_tokens":"8192","max_batch_tokens":"4096"}}'
rolling-restart deploy/runtime-pool-us-west-2
```
mike: also throttling long requests at the gateway: adding a soft cap to long-request-concurrency=8 for now.
sophie: can we temporarily prioritize short requests? maybe change scheduler fairness weight.
dave: applied a scheduler override:
```
POST /admin/scheduler/override
{"policy":"fairness","weight_short":3,"weight_long":1}
```
infra-bot: scheduler override accepted. Node pressure easing on 3/5 hosts.
elaine: after hotfix p95 down to ~220ms in 2m; p99 ~780ms. kv_pages_in/s down to 75. Good trend but still above baseline.
raj: need to follow up with a longer fix: prevent cache blowups by bounding per-tenant KV prefetch and limit per-request KV prefetch depth.
lisa: noted. I'll open an RFC. Also we should run a replay test to reproduce mixed workload fairness issues.
mike: quick mitigation + customer communication: support, can you send a templated incident note? include ETA for rollback to baseline.
support: sending initial notice to impacted customers now, cc product and accounts.
elaine: on-call handoff scheduled in 45m — @mike will take second shift. I'll leave a status update in the channel and a short runbook section.
elaine: runbook snippet to include:
- identify hosts with kv_cache_entries > 8M
- patch batching-config max_window_tokens -> 8k
- set scheduler fairness weight_short=3
- monitor p95 < 400ms and pages_in/s < 100
mike: taking over in 45m. if we see any regression after reverting hotfix, revert override and scale pool horizontally: scale=+2 nodes.
sophie: created an incident tag: INC-2026-KV-BATCH-FAIRNESS. I'll own the postmortem.
raj: for root cause hypothesis: continuous batching prefetch combined with long-context LLMs -> huge KV writes and background eviction thrash, causing NVMe paging and advertiser of long requests grabbing most batch slots.
dlave (typo intentionally to simulate quick chat): also saw many short requests getting queued behind a single huge request that occupied the batch for 400ms.
elaine: concrete followups:
- short-term: keep hotfix until we can validate per-tenant caps (owners: dave, lisa) — target 6h
- medium-term: scheduler rewrite to pref-weight short/latency-sensitive requests (owner: raj) — target 2 weeks
- long-term: KV prefetch adaptation based on runtime memory and request mix (owner: sophie) — target 6 weeks
infra-bot: autoscale recommendation triggered: add 2 nodes to pool-us-west-2; will proceed in 5m.
dave: scaling now -> kubectl scale deployment/runtime-pool-us-west-2 --replicas=8
infra-bot: scale succeeded. new nodes joining; pages_in/s continuing to fall.
elaine: monitoring shows gradual recovery. I'll update the incident status to mitigated once stable for 15m.
mike: noted — I'll watch the nightly traffic patterns to ensure no regressions on mixed workloads.
support: updated customers: initial mitigation applied, working on longer fix, next update in 3h.
sophie: adding reproducer in staging with traffic mix: 80% short 20% long with bursty arrivals to exercise scheduler fairness.
elaine: thanks team. leaving detailed handoff log for @mike. Marking: Incident severity: Sev2 -> currently mitigated but not resolved. Handoff notes included above.
